findings.title: systemctl stand-in runs the quoted ExecStart literally, so the install scenario can never start the real daemon (AC-5/AC-6)
findings.scenario: T8 wrote ExecStart="%h/.local/bin/vr-talex" (packaging/vr-talex.service:15, quoted). The T9 shim takes it with sed (line 30), giving the string "/home/u/.local/bin/vr-talex" with the double quotes still in it, then runs it unquoted with $cmd (line 32). Bash does not remove quotes that come out of an expansion, so it tries to run a file whose name starts with a quote: 'No such file or directory'. install.sh health_check then times out on gdbus wait org.fcitx.Fcitx5, dies and rolls back, so AC-5 reports FAIL every time it runs with a built daemon. This was never caught because QC checked AC-5/AC-6 only at file/keyfile level (05_qc_report.md:139-140) and the scenario never ran end to end.
findings.fix_hint: In the shim, strip one pair of surrounding double quotes after the %h substitution (cmd=${cmd#\"}; cmd=${cmd%\"}) and run it as "$cmd". Then run the install scenario once with the release binary and record it in the QC report.

findings.title: The shim's stop does not wait for the daemon to exit, unlike systemctl, so the fcitx5 restore check in AC-6 is flaky
findings.scenario: uninstall.sh calls restore_all, which runs 'systemctl --user disable --now vr-talex' (common.sh:401). The real systemctl waits until the process has exited. The shim only sends SIGTERM and returns. restore_all then calls has_owner org.fcitx.Fcitx5 (common.sh:430) while the daemon is still in tasks.shutdown() and still owns the name, so it skips 'fcitx5 -d'. AC-6 then reports 'fcitx5 not running again' even though the product is correct.
findings.fix_hint: In stop(), after kill -TERM, wait for the process to exit (timeout 10 tail --pid=$pid -f /dev/null), as systemd does.

findings.title: No display in the user manager's environment makes fe-ibus return Ok(()), and the daemon then runs and reports READY without the IBus route for the whole session, with no retry (uncertain: depends on when the session exports WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY)
findings.scenario: fe-ibus reads WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY once, from the environment of the systemd user manager. If the unit starts before they are imported, Config::from_env returns None and run returns Ok(()). main.rs:215 counts that as 'not needed': the IBus frontend is removed, fe-fcitx keeps running and READY=1 is sent. No address file is ever written, and gnome-shell (and Qt apps on the IBus route) get no engine until the next restart or login. Nothing is logged, and systemd sees a healthy unit. Two ways in: the unit can be started early by D-Bus activation of org.fcitx.Fcitx5 (SystemdService=vr-talex.service), or by 'systemctl --user start' from a context without the imported variables. A user manager on a graphical target always has a display, so 'not needed' should not be inferred there.
findings.fix_hint: Under systemd (NOTIFY_SOCKET set), treat a missing display as Err (static text) so that Restart=always retries once the session has exported it. Alternatively, keep fe-ibus waiting (re-reading the environment through the manager) instead of returning Ok(()). At least eprintln a static line when the frontend skips itself.

findings.title: A permanent fast failure exhausts StartLimitBurst in about 11 s, and the unit then stays failed after the cause is gone, despite the 'Restart forever' comment
findings.scenario: Restart=always, RestartSec=1, StartLimitBurst=10 in 60 s. One trigger is a vr-talex the user started by hand (it holds $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/vr-talex/ibus.lock): each unit start fails in milliseconds with 'fe-ibus: another instance is running' (server.rs:61, then main.rs:222 exits FAILURE). Another is a ~/.config/ibus/bus that a dotfile manager made a symlink, which write_address_file refuses (Unsafe). After 10 attempts the unit is start-limit-hit. When the manual instance exits, or the cause is otherwise fixed, nothing starts the unit again: D-Bus activation through SystemdService is refused too. Keys stay raw for the rest of the session until the user runs systemctl by hand.
findings.fix_hint: Use backoff instead of a hard stop: StartLimitIntervalSec=0 with RestartSec=1, RestartSteps=5, RestartMaxDelaySec=30 (systemd 254+, Ubuntu 24.04 ships 255). Or, for PrepareError::Running, wait on the lock (blocking lock on the blocking pool) instead of failing.

findings.title: restore_all stops the unit while the D-Bus activation shadow (SystemdService=vr-talex.service) is still installed, so a client call in that window starts vr-talex again and leaves it orphaned (uncertain reachability)
findings.scenario: restore_all first runs 'disable --now' (line 401). It removes $DBUS_SVC_DST and reloads the bus only later (restore_entry, then reload_bus at line 422). 'disable' does not block a start. A method call to org.fcitx.Fcitx5 in that window that may auto-start (for example a fcitx-route app re-probing after the name vanished) makes the bus start vr-talex.service again. daemon-reload then drops the unit file, but the process keeps running and owns org.fcitx.Fcitx5 and the IBus address files. 'systemctl --user start fcitx5' and 'fcitx5 -d' then fail to get the names, and uninstall warns 'fcitx5 did not start' with vr-talex still serving.
findings.fix_hint: Restore or remove the D-Bus service file and call reload_bus before stopping the unit. Or run 'systemctl --user mask --runtime vr-talex.service' before 'disable --now' and unmask at the end.
